rounds.fact: Gawker built its identity on gossipy, irreverent media and tech coverage, and its comment sections were an early influential experiment in giving readers real visibility on a media site.
Kickstarter launched in 2009 and popularized the all-or-nothing crowdfunding model, where projects only get funded if they hit their goal, a rule meant to protect backers.
eBaum's World built its early traffic on hosting viral videos and flash animations, and was frequently accused of re-uploading other creators' content without credit.
LiveJournal was one of the first blogging platforms to build in a real social layer, with friends lists and privacy settings, making it feel more like an early social network than a simple blog host.
Napster's original file-sharing service was sued into shutting down in 2001, but the brand survived and was later relaunched as a legal paid streaming service.
